claims.text: Robert Bigelow founded the National Institute for Discovery Science and purchased Skinwalker Ranch in 1996 for $200,000.

claims.text: The ranch is approximately 512 acres in Uintah County, Utah; Bigelow purchased it for $200,000 in 1996 and sold it for approximately $500,000 in 2016 to Brandon Fugal, who announced ownership in March 2020 via Adamantium Real Estate LLC.

claims.sourceText: Wikipedia, Skinwalker Ranch, citing Reid's and Lacatski's accounts
claims.text: DIA official James Lacatski contacted Bigelow after reading 'Hunt for the Skinwalker' and reported an experience at the ranch; Bigelow relayed this to Sen. Harry Reid, and Reid and Sen. Ted Stevens subsequently secured approximately $22 million in Defense appropriations to study unidentified aerial phenomena.
NIDS investigators including retired Army Col. John B. Alexander examined close to 100 incidents at the ranch but acknowledged difficulty obtaining evidence consistent with scientific publication.

claims.sourceText: Wikipedia, Skinwalker Ranch — DEMOTED from Tier 1 (cited to a secondary/encyclopedic source); needs primary replacement
claims.text: Skinwalker Ranch lies in Uintah County, Utah, southeast of Ballard, bordering the Uintah and Ouray Indian Reservation; UFO reports from the Uintah Basin were publicised beginning in the 1970s.

a.label: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)

edges.label: The AAWSAP appropriation followed the Lacatski visit to the ranch
edges.note: Reid and Sen. Ted Stevens secured roughly $22 million in Defense appropriations after Bigelow relayed Lacatski's ranch experience. BAASS, headquartered in Las Vegas, won the contract.

edges.label: Lacatski's visit is the documented link from the ranch to DIA
edges.note: Lacatski contacted Bigelow after reading 'Hunt for the Skinwalker', visited the ranch and reported an experience there; Bigelow relayed this to Sen. Harry Reid.

edges.label: NIDS ran the field investigation at the ranch under Bigelow
edges.note: NIDS investigators including retired Army Col. John B. Alexander examined close to 100 incidents while conceding they could not obtain publishable evidence.

edges.label: purchased the ranch in 1996 and owned it throughout the DIA contract
edges.note: The Deseret News reported the sale in June 1996 and Bigelow confirmed in August 1998 that the Shermans had agreed as a condition of purchase to keep quiet about what they had witnessed.

edges.label: The ranch sits inside the Uintah Basin reporting region
edges.note: The property is in Uintah County southeast of Ballard, bordering the Uintah and Ouray Indian Reservation, inside a region with a folk reporting record dating to the 1970s.
